name: @guardbee/mcp-oauth-auditor
description: MCP server that scans an MCP server's own authorization code for OAuth 2.1 anti-patterns named in the MCP spec's Security Considerations: token passthrough, missing audience validation, OAuth/OIDC discovery SSRF, missing PKCE, loose redirect_uri validation, and hardcoded client secrets
long_description: The MCP specification's Security Considerations section names token passthrough (forwarding a client's token to a downstream API unchanged instead of exchanging/re-scoping it) and missing audience validation (accepting a token whose aud claim was never issued for this server) as the central authorization risks for an MCP server acting as an OAuth resource server. This package scans a server's own authorization/token-handling code for those two patterns, plus three related anti-patterns: an OAuth/OIDC discovery document fetched from a client-supplied URL (the shape behind CVE-2026-45609, an SSRF via OAuth discovery), an authorization request missing PKCE (required by OAuth 2.1 for every client type), redirect_uri validated with a prefix/substring check instead of an exact match (open-redirect bypass), and a hardcoded OAuth client_secret. No API key required — runs entirely locally, static analysis only.
